html:
The Kokoberra are an Aboriginal Australian people of the western Cape York Peninsula, near the mouth of the Mitchell River on the Gulf of Carpentaria. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country is wetlands, river channels and coastal plains. Today many Kokoberra live at Kowanyama, which began as an Anglican mission on the Mitchell River in 1905 and is shared with the Yir Yoront and Kunjen. Neighbours on the map include the Kok Narr, the Thaayorre and the Kunjen. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
